background_notes.fact: Standard Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n has measurable open sets and is finite on compact sets for every natural n.

grounds.reason: Xn is finite-dimensional standard Euclidean space.
dx is its standard Lebesgue measure.
These are the ambient measurable-topology and local-finiteness conditions for the supplied M001 signature.

background_notes.justification: Open subsets are Borel and therefore Lebesgue measurable. A compact subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space is bounded and lies in a cube [-R,R]^n for some finite R>0. The cube has finite Lebesgue volume (2R)^n, so monotonicity gives finiteness on the compact subset. In dimension zero the space is a single point with standard volume one, giving the same conclusion.
